fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. The verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" The speaker has just been praising wisdom, and here the LORD founded the earth by it. The same verse says He "…established the heavens by understanding."

Strength is a fair guess, friend, but the verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" The word is wisdom, the very thing the speaker has been praising since verse 13. Strength isn't the word in this verse.

Doorposts do show up elsewhere in the Bible, in Deuteronomy 6:9, but not here. In this verse the speaker says to write them "…on the tablet of your heart." The writing goes inside the person, friend, not on the house.
Careful, baker, this one has a catch. The speaker says that holding on to these things brings "…favor and high regard in the sight of God and man." That's God AND people, so the answer is False.

Testing sounds like poking a cookie to see if it's done, friend, and that's not what this verse asks. It says, "…in all your ways acknowledge Him…" Acknowledging means recognizing Him, not checking whether He passes.

Yes, baker. Instead of being wise in his own eyes, the son is told to "fear the LORD and turn away from evil." That's the swap: quit acting like you've got it all figured out and look up instead. I've read my own recipe, said "I know better," and had the dough set me straight.

True, baker. The verse says the LORD disciplines the one He loves, "…as does a father the son in whom he delights." A father who delights in his son and still disciplines him. I know a thing or two about that picture.

Not in her hands, baker. The verse says, "Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor." Both hands are already full, and strength isn't in either one. I'd look for a third hand, but the verse only gives her two.

It's True, friend. The verse says, "All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful." The question mentioned peaceful first, but the verse gives you both. Pleasant is right there in the first half.
Fire makes for a dramatic guess, baker, but that's not the word. The verse says, "The LORD founded the earth by wisdom…" It's the same wisdom the speaker has been praising since verse 13.
